review_note: Independent Claude (anthropic/claude-sonnet-5) review. Core keys confirmed correct by independently opening primary sources: Hara=Noriko (BFI Tokyo Story), Bergman=Ilsa (BFI Casablanca), Redding wrote/first recorded Respect 1965, Franklin 1967 (LOC blog), Dixon wrote Hoochie Coochie Man for Waters (LOC PDF metadata + established fact). No answer-meaning change needed. REWORK items: (1) FACTUAL ERROR in cinema-02 distractor_reasoning and article body: 'Мадлен Эльстер' is claimed to be 'another Bergman role' / from Notorious — false. Independently verified via BFI's own 'Ingrid Bergman: 10 essential films' list (no Vertigo) plus general knowledge: Madeleine Elster is Kim Novak's character in Hitchcock's Vertigo, not an Ingrid Bergman role at all. Fix the article sentence ('Имена Мадлен, Алисия и Паула относятся к другим ролям Бергман') and the distractor_reasoning entry, or swap this distractor for a genuine Bergman role (e.g. Karin from Autumn Sonata). (2) cinema-01 article claims Noriko is 'вдова их погибшего на войне сына' (war-widow detail); neither cited BFI nor Criterion URL states this per my independent fetch of the BFI page (confirms root's observation). Add a supporting citation or remove/soften the claim. (3) cinema-02 wording 'позже героиня оказывается женой... Ласло' implies the marriage happened after/because of the Paris affair; BFI's own description uses present tense ('now the wife of a resistance leader') — she is already married when the rekindled affair is shown. Reword to avoid false chronology (confirms root's concern independently). (4) sources-v1.md overstates access: I independently attempted the second music-02 LOC registry-overview URL and got HTTP 403 Forbidden; root independently got 'Internal Error' on the same URL. Two independent reviewers failed to open it — sources-v1.md's claim that 'all eight URLs were actually opened' is not accurate for this one. Downgrade its role to uncorroborated context, not a verified second source. Access/claim-support documentation otherwise solid; no invented citations found elsewhere.
